implementation_notes: Rust enforces the pattern's core by default: struct fields are private unless marked `pub`, and the Rust API guidelines list 'Structs have private fields' (C-STRUCT-PRIVATE) precisely because a public field 'prevents the type from providing any validation or maintaining any invariants on the contents of the field, since clients can mutate it arbitrarily'. Reads return a borrowed shared slice - `fn courses(&self) -> &[Course]` - or an iterator (`self.courses.iter()`); mutation goes through `&mut self` methods, so an aliased mutable collection is unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. The classic accessor plumbing is only still needed to hide the concrete container type or to return an owned snapshot (`to_vec()`); `pub courses: Vec<Course>` or a Deref/DerefMut newtype is the Rust spelling of the leaking getter.
pitfalls: `&[Course]` borrows the field for the caller's scope, so the slice cannot be held across an add_course call - that is the guarantee, but it forces narrow borrow scopes and sometimes a to_vec() at API boundaries.
Returning `&Vec<Course>` leaves mutation impossible but publishes the representation; prefer `&[T]`, and beware Deref/DerefMut impls on newtype wrappers, which re-expose the whole container.
A `pub` field or public tuple-struct field removes every invariant at once; framework derives (serde Serialize with a public field, reflection-style ORMs) are the common accidental escape hatch.
Slices share their elements: membership is protected, but interior mutability (Cell/RefCell/Mutex inside elements) can still change element state through a shared borrow.
